articleTitle: Development of High-Density Hybrid Substrate for Heterogeneous Integration
abstract: The fan-out chip-last panel-level packaging for chiplets heterogeneous integration is investigated. Emphasis is placed on the design, materials, process, and fabrication of a high-density organic hybrid substrate using an interconnect-layer.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Half-Bridge Power Module with POL-kW
abstract: In recent years, SiC & GaN, so-called a wide bandgap (WBG) power devices, have begun to be introduced into the market. More sophisticated packaging technology to maximize the performance of WBG devices are required accordingly. Power-Overlay-kilo-Watt (POL-kW) is an advanced package for high power applications. Physical model scale comparison of power modules between employing the POL-kW and the existing package demonstrated the electrical and thermal advantage of POL-kW. Compared to Half-bridge power module with POL-kW and existing package, the module with POL-kW offered 50% volume reduction, 20% thermal conductivity improvement, and lower turn off surge voltage were realized.

articleTitle: 3D Metal Printed Deformed Elliptical Cavity Bandpass Filter with an Additional Plate
abstract: This paper presents a modified deformed elliptical cavity resonator. 5-pole bandpass filter was designed, and 3D printed using Selective Laser Melting (SLM) as a prototype. The measured results have a relatively good agreement with simulated ones.

articleTitle: A rapid COVID-19 diagnostic device integrating porous microneedles and the paper-based immunoassay biosensor
abstract: New coronavirus, SARS-CoV-2, named as COVID-19 was identified and caused the global pandemic in 2020. Recent challenging issues include providing users with non-invasive and easy-to-use diagnostic devices and identifying the infected to prevent the spread of COVID-19 as quick as possible. In this study, a new COVID-19 diagnostic device that integrates porous microneedles (MNs) with a paper-based immunoassay biosensor was developed for the rapid antibody detection. The biodegradable porous MNs made of polylactic acid (PLA) were fabricated and used to extract the interstitial fluid (ISF) in the human skin by capillary effect. The extracted ISF was flowed into the immunoassay biosensor, which results in the detection of SARS-CoV-2 antibodies on site. From In vitro tests, the result demonstrated that human anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgM and IgG could be detected within 2 min. It is expected that COVID-19 can be diagnosed fast and painlessly owing to the porous MNs as well as a paper sensor with the short flow distance between MNs and a sensor. Besides COVID-19, the proposed device has great potential in the fast screening of various kinds of infectious diseases as an effective complementary method with other diagnostic tests.

articleTitle: Effect of Surface Treatment of Transmission Line on Frequency Characteristics
abstract: Because of the considerable increase in internet traffic, the bitrate of optical transceivers has increased. In recent years, 56 Gbps (28 Gbaud PAM4) interfaces have already been deployed for commercial use, and 112 Gbps (56 Gbaud PAM4) signals have begun to be discussed by several standard development organizations. With increase in the bitrate, technologies for accurately analyzing the effects of the surface treatment of transmission lines on printed circuit boards are becoming more important. This is due to the fact that at high frequencies, the skin effect, in which the current concentrates on the surface of the pattern, becomes relatively significant. This study fabricated test boards for measuring transmission lines with three types of surface treatments, which were plated with only Cu foil, ENEPIG, and IGEPIG. The transmission lines were measured using a VNA and high-frequency probes. The validity of results was confirmed using an electromagnetic field simulator based on the finite-difference time-domain method.

articleTitle: Silver sintering technology based on induction heating for chip level bonding
abstract: This paper presents a method for rapid and homogeneous induction heating of micro-scaled silver particle layers to support and enhance the bonding process of microelectronic components at the chip level.

articleTitle: 3D Metal Printed Corrugated Waveguide Antenna Array With High Gain and Enhanced Bandwidth
abstract: In this paper, wideband corrugated waveguide slot antenna arrays using higher-order modes are investigated. The metal 3D printing technology was used to fabricate the model, and the tested results agreed well with simulated ones.

articleTitle: Abnormal-state-discrimination Method for In-vehicle Communication Channel with Power-over-Coax Circuit
abstract: We propose an abnormal-state-discrimination method for the in-vehicle communication channel with a power-over-coax (PoC) circuit. The proposed method uses digital data, such as equalizer parameters and error information, that can be obtained from general serializer/deserializer large-scale integrated circuits. Therefore, no additional components are required to diagnose the abnormal state of the channel. We specifically focus on detecting an anomaly of a PoC filter.

articleTitle: Creating Low Thermal Resistance Interfaces in Wide Bandgap Semiconductors Through Bonding
abstract: The thermal resistance at interfaces in wide bandgap semiconductors can impact the overall thermal resistance in junction temperature in devices. However, the resistance that exists at interfaces are impacted by the integration methods that arise from growth and or device manufacturing. In this work, we report the use of plasma activated bonding to create ultralow thermal resistance interfaces between WBG semiconductors (GaN and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${Ga_{2}O_{3}}$</tex>) and high thermal conductivity substrates (SiC, Diamond). Thermal boundary conductance was measured using time domain thermoreflectance and showed that the TBC is as high as 230 MW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>K for GaN on SiC and up to 90 MW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>K for GaN on diamond. These results represent the some of the highest performing thermal interfaces for these materials systems and are enabled using a wafer scale compatible bonding process.

articleTitle: Densely Integrated 1060nm 2D VCSEL Array for Space-division Multiplexing Toward Co-packaging Optics Transceivers
abstract: A densely integrated 16-channel VCSEL array was demonstrated with good single mode characteristics at 1060 nm-band. A coupling loss of 3.0dB was obtained experimentally which can be decreased below 1dB after optimizing the VCSEL MFD.

articleTitle: Connection Characteristics of Hollow-Core Fiber Connector
abstract: A hollow-core fiber connector is proposed that uses a ferrule with an angled cavity as a thin protective glass plate. It can typically realize 0.5-dB attenuation and a 50-dB return loss without physical contact.

articleTitle: Multi-Gigabit/s LiFi Networking for 6G
abstract: We show that the optical spectrum can be used to build terabit per second (Tbps) secure wireless access networks. Two fundamental advantages of this spectrum are: 1) there are off-the-shelf transmitter and receiver devices that can be used today, and 2) this spectrum is completely unregulated and free. We conclude that in 6G wireless access networks we will witness a paradigm shift from RF to optical.

articleTitle: Noise Reduction Termination for RFI Induced Channel Resonance using Common-mode Choke and Differential Signal Balancer
abstract: The impact of the channel resonance due to the external RF noise is analyzed for the differential transmission line sandwiched between the common-mode filters (CMFs). The channel resonance causes a differential noise by the mode conversion. We confirm that the problem of the channel resonance can be removed by the differential signal balancer embedded in the metal layer of silicon LSI (DSB-EIM). The combination of DSB-EIM and a common-mode choke coil (CMC) can effectively remove external RF noise.

articleTitle: Application of a Polymer Microlens with a Pillar for High Efficiency Coupling between Single Mode Fibers and SiPh Chips
abstract: Recently, silicon photonics technology has attracted significant attention. However, low coupling efficiency, due to the difference in spot size between silicon photonic (SiPh) chips and single-mode fibers (SMFs), remains a challenging issue. To solve this problem, most coupling devices reported thus far are fabricated on the end face of an SMF. This study proposes a novel approach, wherein a new coupling device is fabricated on the end face of the SiPh chip to increase the spot size of the output light from the SiPh chip. Moreover, the test samples, fabricated using UV-curable resin, are evaluated. The design details are introduced herein.

articleTitle: Reliability and Bend Loss of Optical Fibers in Tight Bend Applications
abstract: Dense optical connectivity applications require optical fibers to be bent at radii as small as 2 mm. We present an updated mechanical reliability model to illustrate that reduced clad fibers will provide acceptable fatigue resistance.

articleTitle: A High Capacity and Cost-Effective OFDM EML TO-CAN for RoF/IFoF Transmission Systems in Beyond-5G Mobile Fronthaul
abstract: We present the feasibility of a cost-effective hermetically sealed EML TO-CAN for RoF/IFoF systems. The results show that a net bit rate of 144 Gbps can be expected by using 45 400-MHz-bandwidth 256QAM OFDM signals.

articleTitle: Interpolation Method for Sparse Point Cloud at Long Distance Using Sensor Fusion with LiDAR and Camera
abstract: LiDAR plays an important role for automated driving systems. However, the limitation of LiDAR is sparse point cloud at a long distance. To solve this problem, we propose a point interpolation method, using sensor fusion with LiDAR and camera.

articleTitle: Characterization of Low Loss Dielectric Materials for 5G Applications
abstract: The dissipation factor and dielectric constant of low loss dielectric materials are measured by the Fabry-Perot open resonator technique. A coplanar waveguide with ground test vehicle is being designed and fabricated. The impedance is measured and the effective dielectric constant of the test vehicle is calculated.

articleTitle: Estimation of Electric Field Radiated from Wire Harness Based on Approximation of Common-Mode Current Distribution Using Asymmetric Dipole Antenna
abstract: In this study, we proposed a method for estimating the radiated electric field from a wire harness based on common-mode current measurements at one position of the wire and an equivalent dipole antenna approximation. The validation of the method was confirmed by simulations and experiments, and the results showed that the peak frequency and field level can be estimated within an estimation error of about 20 MHz and 8 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Measurement of Poisson's Ratio of Resin Materials
abstract: Poisson's ratio is a typical physical property value of materials along with Young's modulus. Poisson's ratio values of various resin samples were measured. Additives for resin modification affect the Poisson's ratio and FEM result.

articleTitle: High-efficiency optical coupling between VCSEL and 90-degree-bent Graded-Index Core Polymer Waveguide with Numeral Aperture Optimization
abstract: In this paper, we propose a higher efficiency optical coupling technique using 90-degree-bent Graded-Index (GI) core polymer waveguide which replaces conventional optical assembly (mirrors and lenses) in vertical cavity surface emitting laser (VCSEL) based optical engines. The 90-degree-bent GI-core polymer waveguides are fabricated using the Mosquito method. However, high coupling loss could be caused by the VCSEL beam divergence due to diffraction in the lens free coupling. We theoretically confirm that total insertion loss including bending loss as well as coupling loss could remain low by the waveguide NA control. Fabricating the 90-degree-bent GI-core polymer waveguides with the optimized NA, a waveguide insertion loss as low as about 2 dB is experimentally achieved.

articleTitle: Tapered Pillar on Single-mode Fiber Facet Fabricated using UV Curable Resin for High Efficiency Coupling to Silicon Photonics Chip
abstract: We propose a novel coupling device with a tapered pillar on a single-mode fiber (SMF) facet for efficient coupling in a silicon photonics chip. A tapered pillar was fabricated using UV-curable resin by a 405 nm laser beam irradiated from a high-NA (HiNA) fiber with a spot size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.1\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> at a wavelength of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.55\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. A coupling efficiency of approximately 60% was obtained between the SMF and a similar HiNA fiber during the fabrication of the taper pillar.

articleTitle: LiDAR for Automated Driving Era
abstract: Because of its high spatial resolution and ability to create high-resolution environmental maps that radar can't, the use of LiDAR for highly automated driving has been resurrected. This paper shows how LiDAR has been treated so far, and introduce the principle of LiDAR and the possibility of solving latency problems that were inferior to radar in the future.

articleTitle: Method of Diagnosing Abnormalities in Bidirectional Communication Channel by Using Adaptive Decision Feedback Equalizer
abstract: Nowadays, as autonomous cars become widely used, it will be even more crucial to maintain their self-diagnosis functions to ensure the reliability of the vehicles. The importance of in-vehicle communication will increase as well, resulting in more frequent maintenance. Moreover, the configuration of autonomous driving systems, which include in-vehicle cables, are becoming increasingly complicated, and replacing all abnormal components for maintenance can be costly and time consuming. In this paper, we propose a new method of diagnosing abnormalities in the communication channel by using the tap information of adaptive DFE (Decision Feedback Equalizer). The method detects the reflected signal and calculates its delay from the abnormal point by superimposing the reflected signal to the transmitted signal in a bidirectional communication channel. We used a simulation to verify that the DFE reacts to the superimposed signal and corresponds to the delay of the reflected signal. The proposed method enables the diagnosis of abnormalities with a resolution of 0.17 m in 1 Gbps bidirectional communication. Thus, by simply replacing the abnormal component, maintenance costs can be reduced.

articleTitle: Feature Detection Based on Virtual Gradient Using Sensor Fusion for Low-resolution 3D LiDAR
abstract: LiDAR plays an indispensable role as recognition sensor for mobile devices, autonomous driving, etc. This paper aims to address Low-resolution LiDARs' sparse data problem via fuse image feature point and pointcloud data.

articleTitle: Development of newly low-dielectric organic substrate material for a millimeter-wave radar
abstract: We have developed a new organic substrate material for high-frequency applications. Printed circuit boards based on the developed material showed low transmission loss characteristics and satisfied the basic reliability requirements of circuit boards.

articleTitle: Biologically Inspired Ultrathin Array Cameras
abstract: Insect eyes have superior visual functions for advanced multi-functional imaging applications. Here we report various microfabrication methods for microlens arrays and an ultrathin arrayed camera for high contrast and high-resolution multifunctional imaging, inspired by the vision system of Xenos peckii. Like insect's multifunctional vision, this ultrathin array camera allows large field-of-view, 3D imaging, high speed imaging, microscopic imaging, and multispectral imaging. This work also includes recent achievements on assorted biomedical applications.

articleTitle: O-Band Silicon-Organic Hybrid EO Modulator
abstract: Short-range optical fiber communication is the key in intra and inter data center network, which is recently required significant improvement in signal processing speed because of the increasing data traffic of video streaming service and many other applications. The electro-optic (EO) polymer modulator is the promising device to be used in such fiber network application because of the advanced modulation performance with low driving voltage and high frequency response. However, previous EO polymer modulators have demonstrated the modulation at the wavelength of 1.55 μm (C-band) because of the optical loss limitation at shorter wavelengths of such as 1.31 μηι (O-band). In this study, we fabricated silicon-organic hybrid modulator for O-band operation by replacing the pervious EO polymer. The modulator consists of the Mach-Zehnder interferometer Si waveguide with a hybrid slot and polymer phase shifter. The measured half-wavelength voltage product (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">π·</inf>L) was 0.56 V·cm. We demonstrate 40 Gbps on-off-keying modulation, and show that the fabricated modulator is promising the higher bit rate signaling for O-band optical fiber communication application.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Pulse Method with Arbitrary Characteristic Impedance for Immunity Evaluation of ESD Protection Device
abstract: In a conventional TLP system, the pulse disturbance is applied to the DUT via the transmission line, whose characteristic impedance is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50\ \Omega$</tex>. However, the DUT for the evaluation, such as an ESD protection device, may be affected by the transmission line's characteristic impedance. This paper adds an impedance matching circuit to the conventional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50\ \Omega$</tex> TLP system, making it possible to adjust the circuit to an arbitrary value of the transmission line's characteristic impedance. By using the developed system, the I-V characteristics of an ESD protection device are evaluated when the characteristic impedance is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20\ \Omega,\ 50\ \Omega$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$150\ \Omega$</tex>. As a result, it was found that the negative resistance characteristics after the breakdown voltage change depending on the transmission line's characteristic impedance.

articleTitle: System Transmission Over Multicore Fiber for Datacom Optical Interconnect Applications
abstract: Measurement and analysis of 100G and/or 400G transmission properties of an 8-core MM-MCF and a 4-core SM-MCF assembly indicate the robustness of the MM-MCF and SM-MCF supporting optical interconnects for intra- and/or inter- datacenters applications.

articleTitle: Fabrication of the electro-optic polymer modulator for O-band intra-datacenter communications
abstract: The electro-optic materials (a)–(d) are molecularly engineered to be applicable for O-band modulator for datacenter communication. The EO material (a) based EO modulator exhibits the smallest driving voltage of 2.8 V which equals to in-device figure of merit <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta^{3}r_{33}$</tex> of 138 pm/V at 1550 nm. This shows the possibility of larger <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta^{3}r_{33}$</tex> at O-band.

articleTitle: Liquid Crystal Polymer Technology in the 5G Era - MetroCirc -
abstract: Liquid crystal polymer (LCP) is an adequate material for flexible printed circuit (FPC) in high frequency applications especially at millimeter wave frequencies. Murata's LCP-FPC: MetroCirc, is manufactured using a unique process that adds unique features to fit high-density 3-dimensional product design. Several application examples of it are shown.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Wafer Bond Strength under Vacuum
abstract: Wafer bonding is a key technology for the integration, packaging, and assembly of the electronic devices. The measurement of the mechanical reliability at the bonding interface should also be reliable in order to evaluate the device reliability and robustness. Here we present a new scheme of the bond strength quantification considering the effect of the measurement atmosphere, especially ambient water. As the water attacks the Si-O-Si bonds at the crack front during the bond strength measurement, we propose the fracture test of the bonded wafers in a sealed chamber based on the double cantilever beam model under the controlled atmosphere. The bond strength is affected by the atmospherics water, indicated by the lowered bond strength in the ambient air compared to the dry N2 gas, which is also supported by the previous studies. In addition, it is also revealed that the bond strength is measured higher under high vacuum. The developed method of bond strength measurement will evaluate not only the effect of the ambient air, but also the effect of the residual water at the bonding interface.

articleTitle: The Electrical Analysis on Ultra High Density IO Fan-Out Design
abstract: With the rapid development of self-driving cars, 5G mobile communications and artificial intelligence (AI), the high performance semiconductor integrated circuits have become a potential product in semiconductor industry. In order to support huge data transmission throughput, the package types play an important role in achieving high bandwidth and low latency. The layout density of traditional Flip Chip BGA (FCBGA) cannot contain thousands of signal lines. In the recent, 2.5D IC package with ultra-high density I/O is able to apply in such high-performance computing product. 2.5D IC has a silicon interposer which is an electrical interface routing to spread a connection to a wider pitch or to reroute the signals. TSV is an import element of interposer in vertical connection between ASIC chips or HBM chips to package substrate. However, it is hard to increase the production yield of the silicon interposer due to the TSV structure. The cost and productivity are also considered in manufacture. Some OSAT (Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test) companies did some studies [1]–[5] and proposed some structures without TSV, such as FOCoS (Fan-out Chip on Substrate). By different process, there are Chip First FOCoS and Chip last FOCoS both are suitable for different applications and production costs [6]. In first part of paper, we introduce the 2.5D IC and FOCoS which are currently package type applied in ultra-high density I/O design. According to real design, the actual structure of high-performance computing IC device with one ASIC die and two HBM dies is shown in this paper. There are different trace lengths and ground plane designs due to different location of HBM die and manufacture issues. Finally, we use eye diagram analysis to estimate the quality of high speed signal.

articleTitle: Automated Photonics Testing at Wafer Level
abstract: Packaging and micro-assembly have long been considered an obstacle to the wide acceptance and mass production of PICs (Photonics Integrated Circuit), promoting the development of hybrid-assembly automated processes like bonding, active fibre optic alignment, and more, with specialised companies taking up the challenge and producing dedicated equipment. Yet another need is now emerging: that of fast, automated, large volume testing of photonics devices. This paper offers an overview of the main issues and ‘ingredients’ of photonics wafer level testing.

articleTitle: Improvement in measurement accuracy of on-wafer measurements from millimeter-wave to Terahertz frequencies
abstract: Device measurement techniques in the millimeterwave (mmW) and THz frequencies are necessary for realizing novel communication technologies such as beyond-5G/6G technologies. Degraded measurement reproducibility is one of the serious problems in those frequencies band. Precision measurement technique, named RF signal detection (RSD) technique, is developed to address the problem. This paper reviews the RSD technique, and reports recent improvements, such as demonstration in the frequencies up to 500 GHz, and with a multi-signal probe.

articleTitle: Technologies for Power Device Packaging by Using Solid Liquid Interdiffusion Bonding - SLID
abstract: This paper presents several approaches for bonding at low temperature with a resulting interface alloy that is stable at temperatures higher than the bonding temperature itself. The bonding principle described herewith is called Solid Liquid Interdiffusion (SLID) bonding, where two metals were used for creating an alloy. First, a low melting point metal defines the process temperature e. g. Sn, In, or Ga. With a high solubility, a second metal forms together with the first metal intermetallic phase(s) during isothermal solidification. By the concentration and the stoichiometric relation of the components the liquid phase while bonding is mainly controlled. This paper will show different material combinations and different deposition technologies for the metals used with regard to efficient fabrication processes.

articleTitle: >25 Gbit/s LiFi with Dual Wavelength Emission, Eye-safe, Laser Based White Light Collimated and Fiber Delivered Light Sources
abstract: We report on high-speed > 25 Gbit/s LiFi (Light Fidelity) communication systems deploying Semipolar GaN laser diode (LD) based single and dual wavelength emission, eye-safe, white light illumination light sources in collimated beam and fiber delivered configurations. Additionally, we report on recent demonstrations of high power Semipolar GaN violet LDs with similar properties to blue LDs described here which have potential for LiFi communications and anti-bacterial optical illumination.

articleTitle: Study of Atomic Layer Deposition of Hafnium Oxide as an Insulation Layer on Cu for Potential Flip Chip Integration
abstract: Ultra thin films of hafnium oxide were deposited on copper using Atomic Layer Deposition. The physical insulation provided by the film was tested using Neutral Salt Spray testing. We examine the role of the thin film in preventing the oxidation of Cu.

articleTitle: Development of 3-Dimensional Single-mode Core Over-Crossing Polymer Optical Waveguides Using the Mosquito Method
abstract: We experimentally represent a 3-dimensional (3D) over-crossing single-mode polymer optical waveguides for onboard optical interconnects. This graded-index (GI) circular core 3D over-crossing structure is developed using the Mosquito method, keeping a height difference at the over-crossing section.

articleTitle: LGA pre Bump Process Elimination
abstract: Land Grid Array (LGA) is a grid array package like Ball Grid Array (BGA) package with terminal pads on bottom surface without solder ball attach to its terminal pads. The electrical connections of LGA are made through bottom terminal pads surface to the terminal pads of Printed Circuit Board (PCB). In Printed Circuit Board Assembly (PCBA) manufacturing process, the typically approach to mount LGA package to PCB are with pre bump LGA and without pre bump. The advantage of pre bump is to have more process margin for improving solder joint (SJ) forming with minimum solder defect such as void, open, and bridging. However, pre bump require additional processes which resulted in negative impact to manufacturing cost and capacity. This paper shares the uniquely designed of LGA stencil aperture “windowpane” to achieve equivalent SJ forming quality without pre bump. With this improvement, the LGA without pre bump can be mounted to PCB using typical Surface Mount Technology (SMT) process along with all the rest of the SMT component.

articleTitle: Novel Approach for Machine Learning with Extra Low Energy and Very Light Hardware
abstract: The editorial committee of The Japan Society of Applied Physics stated an opinion that “after a few decades, electricity consumption for the AI execution systems would constitute drastically more than half of total worldwide ones, at least if we continue to adopt the von Neumann architecture”. The SNN and neuromorphic architectures would be a reality in the near future with very low power consumption. However, these architectures need to build on the society's infrastructure system. Easily reconfigurable architecture should be realized in the market quickly. This object would be focused on our study. Our architecture called VaCoAl (Vague Coincident Architecture) is a target to eliminate drastically power consumption with light hardware like as commercially available stand-alone equipment as the Raspberry Pi and such. That needs no requirement of the new infrastructure for operation of any AI issue because of its novel search engine architecture that is called LPHV-CAM (Low Power High Volume-Content Addressable Memory). This system concept is structured to search for the extracting vague objects and major decision from the extractions. It just can do additional learning in exactly real-time due to the concept. The extracted items are shown to be distinguished with probability percentage values that makes it possible to perform reasoning.

Author Keywords: low energy and light hardware architecture

articleTitle: Improve inductive contact failure loss of IGBT module test
abstract: Smaller and more efficient EV-motor control is accelerating, and IGBT packaging that controls motor driving is evolving remarkably. In particular, IGBT continues to invest in developing compact, high-efficiency packages with a capacity of 100kW or less. For this reason, DC/AC characterization at high power as well as thermal measures affecting efficiency has been incorporated in mass production sites. This paper summarizes the degree of influence of the contactor of the device on stray inductance measurement of IGBT module, and how much the influence can be reduced to measure stray inductance of the module itself with high reliability. Improved yield loss by contact failure is also described.

articleTitle: Control of Electrical Behavior of Stretchable Films Printed Using Electrically Conductive Pastes During Cyclic Tensions
abstract: Electrical conductivity variation of stretchable wires printed with polyurethane-based electrically conductive pastes was examined during a cyclic tensile test. The electrical behavior depends on mechanical properties of the elastomer substrates. Electrical resistivity of the wires can increase during unloading as well as during loading. Deformation of conducting contacts between fillers during unloading governed the increase in electrical resistivity during the cyclic tensile test. Modification of binder chemistry for the electrically conductive pastes will be useful to stabilize electrical conductivity of stretchable printed wires.

articleTitle: Optical Interconnect Ecosystems and Challenges in Co-Packaged Optics
abstract: In this paper we report on the future optical interconnect eco-system required by CPO technologies at the chip, board and system level.

articleTitle: Narrow-bandpass filter using orthogonally propagating guided-mode resonance with doubly periodic grating
abstract: A two-dimensional grating with a doubly periodic structure is proposed to provide a narrow-bandpass filter of a small aperture. The peak transmittance of 96% was obtained by numerical simulation for a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$45-\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>-diameter beam and an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$85-\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>-size filter.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of Y-branched Polymer Waveguide based Optical Coupler
abstract: We propose multiplexer devices in short wavelength range wavelength division multiplexing (SWDM) and mode division multiplexing (MDM) systems as applications of graded-index core Y-branched polymer waveguides. We demonstrate 25-Gbps optical signal transmissions at wavelengths of 850 nm and 1060 nm over an MMF via a Y-branched waveguide as an SWDM multiplexer (MUX) device. For an MDM MUX device, a few-mode scale asymmetric Y-branched waveguide is experimentally fabricated and the optical fields of multiple modes transmitted in the waveguide are confirmed.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Antenna-in-Package Design Validation Solution in Wireless Communication Applications
abstract: In this paper, the 2 by 2 mmWave AiP array is design in organic substrate using fcCSP structure. The RF die is placed on bottom side of organic substrate and the AiP array is put in the front side of organic substrate. Through 3D electromagnetic solver, the single AiP has good bandwidth with over 6dBi antenna gain. In design stage, the spherical chamber is utilized to validate single antenna performance. It can directly probe by RF probe on C4 bump pad or micro bump pad to get 2D or 3D radiation pattern of single antenna. From the simulation and measurement results, there is a good correlation. In engineering stage, the RF die is mounted on the bottom of organic substrate. The AiP device can utilize the compact antenna test range (CATR) chamber to get all relative radiation patterns, such as 2D/3D pattern and EIRP. Of course, the CART is a good validation solution for beamforming measurement. Finally, for mass production, a measurement test set is announced for mmWave AiP or SiP production test. Through the three different measurement solutions and mmWave measurement flow, a completed mmWave AiP and SiP flow from design to validation is delivered.

articleTitle: Practical Simulation Methods Considering Characteristic Variations of Wires for CISPR 25 Conducted Emission
abstract: A method to predict the test results about CISPR 25 without detailed information is proposed. This method could be adaptable for changes of wire types, numbers, and placement topologies. It was confirmed that this method can correspond to the filter difference of DUTs. The average error between simulation and measurements were 4.07 dB with coupled transmission line wire model and 1.28 dB with extracted from measurements wire model in the FM radio band, respectively. This wire modeling methods could be adapted to other tests.

articleTitle: Electrical Conductivity of Air-curable Electrically Conductive Adhesives Containing Copper Fillers Using Mixed Surfactants
abstract: Effect of surfactants on electrical conductivity of copper-filled adhesives composed of resol-type phenolic resin was investigated. The adhesives containing copper fillers treated with oleic acid and mono ethanol amine showed relatively low electrical resisivities after curing in air. Moreover, electrical conductivity of the adhesives can be further enhanced by simultaneously using these surfactants for surface treatment of the fillers. Magnitude of the enhancement of electrical conductivity by the surfactant mixtures was different depending on composition of the mixtures. Interface chemistry between fillers will be a key for establish materials designs for advanced copper-filled adhesives.

articleTitle: Functional interfaces for an openable artificial intestinal tract device as an organ-on-a-chip
abstract: We report the functional interfaces packaging the artificial intestinal tract device, which is an organ-on-a-chip. By packaging the interface, it becomes possible to perform a 120 minutes perfusion experiment while maintaining the conventional perfusion experiment function.

articleTitle: Precise thixotropy controlled Bump Support Film for WLCSP
abstract: This research focuses on the application of the resin with fluidity to the uneven surface of bump wafers. We have solved the problem of staining that occurs when pouring resin by controlling the thixotropy of the material.

articleTitle: Multi-modal Thin-Film-Transistor Biosensing Platforms for Bio-medical Investigations: Contribution to Internet-of-Medical-Things
abstract: The great evolution of device technology, wireless systems, and artificial intelligence is bringing tremendous and deep change in the field of biomedical. This transformation is participating to the Internet of Medical Things revolution. But, biomedical analyses devices are still limited to not portable devices, single analyses technique or poor spatial sensing. In our research, we used Thin-Film-Transistor technology to realize devices with multi-modal sensing possibility, and with high spatial sensing. We report the results obtained with these devices applied to various sensing and manipulation techniques on biological cells, like dielectrophoresis, electrophysiology, bioimpedance, or electrochemistry. It is expected that they participate to development of digital health.

articleTitle: Modeling of Polarization-Rotation Based All-Optical Logic Switch Using Ring-Resonator
abstract: In this paper, an all-optical polarization rotation based ring-resonator has been modeled to realize all-optical logical NOT gate. The azimuth angle of polarization state has been altered with the requirement of low pump power.

articleTitle: Mode-Confined Ultra Thin Silicon/Polymer Hybrid Electro-Optic Modulator
abstract: In this letter, we report an electro-optic (EO) modulator consisted of the silicon waveguide with the EO polymer cladding. In the hybrid waveguide the TE0 mode is highly confined around the silicon core. Thus, we obtained relatively small half-wave-voltage length product (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">π</inf>L) of 2.15 V·cm. The measured V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">π</inf>L is 28% smaller than the value obtained from standard polymer waveguide modulator. In addition, the hybrid structure possesses a propagation loss of 0.46 dB/mm in phase shifter part.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Flexible Polyimide Fibers for Dense Optical Packaging
abstract: We have demonstrated a flexible polyimide fiber as an optical waveguide from soluble 6-6 polyimide. The diameter of this fiber reached to 30 μ m, and with flexibility of 3mm diameter. It shows transmission loss less than 0.1dB/cm with polyimide cladding layer and has observed clear single-TEM00-mode-pattern after 3cm transmission.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Analysis of Surface Oxide Layers of Various Copper Films in Microelectronics
abstract: Copper is a commonly used conductor and metallization materials. However, surface copper oxide layers which readily form during fabrication and assembly processes will increase electrical/thermal resistance, and even cause reliability problems. The dominating factors include the constituent phases of surface oxide layer, as well as the thickness ratio of CuO/Cu2O. The most common way to analyze surface oxide layer are XPS (X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy) and TEM (Transmission electron microscopy) techniques. However, sophisticated instruments are required and sample preparation is time-consuming. Efficient and accurate on-line or at-line measurement is very crucial. In this study, the analysis of oxidized layer of electroplated, and cold-rolled copper surface by means of coulometric reduction method was developed. Various microelectronic assembly processes were simulated to obtain copper surface with different oxidation conditions, including molding, curing, reflowing, and high temperature aging were also performed. Experimental results demonstrate that coulometric reduction can precisely detect the oxide phase and their thickness regardless of the sample conditions.

articleTitle: Development of the h-BN manufacturing process for 3D-LSI
abstract: Hexagonal-BN (h-BN) based SOI structure with through silicon via (TSV) shows higher heat dissipation performance without degrading electrical characteristics compared with the conventional SOI structure. This paper evaluates the manufacturing process for 3D-LSI concluding h-BN. Hexagonal-BN etched by F2+ He shows useful top shapes of TSV for the 3D-LSI.

articleTitle: Gold Coated Optical Microneedles Lens Array for Photothermal Therapy
abstract: Photothermal therapy has been widely used for the treatment of skin disease such as Telangiectasia or skin cancer due to the profound benefit because of the noninvasiveness and selectivity. However, due to the limited penetration of light in skin tissue with the presence of melanin, safe and effective photothermal therapy using laser becomes challenging when the photon interacts with other biomolecule before reaching the target. Therefore, we proposed an Optical Microneedle Lens Array (OMLA) coated with gold to improve photothermal therapy efficiency. This device plays a role of light guiding so that it can deliver photon at target precisely.

articleTitle: Modification of Polyurethane-based Binder for Stabilizing Electrical Conductivity of Silver-filled Stretchable Printed Wires During Cyclic Tensions
abstract: This paper discussed effect of binder chemistry on electrical conductivity variation due to tensile deformation of stretchable wires and electrodes that were printed with polyurethane-based electrically conductive pastes containing silver micro-flakes. Although their electrical conductivity usually showed a significant variation during uniaxial cyclic tensions, use of some polyurethane-based binders, including polyhydroxyurethane, were found to be effective to suppress the electrical conductivity variation. Binder chemistry is believed to be one of the important factors in development of novel electrically conductive pastes for printing stretchable wires and electrodes.
